description.narrative: Masarouna mobilizes the power of young people in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) so they can claim their sexual and reproductive health and rights. We work with and for young people, and together we forge new pathways to create meaningful and sustainable change. Masarouna is a 5-year program funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

comment.narrative: In the Mutual Capacity Strengthening (CATool) 2022, in relation to civic space influencing capacities, new "both women and youth led" partners expressed an interest in strengthening their capacity on understanding and navigating (offline and online) civic space for young people working on SRHR; civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, partners and people we work with; protection in digital space; health and wellbeing; perception by & relation with constituency; and strengthening/broadening partnerships (movements & coalitions). Partners also indicated that they are currently providing support to others on civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, partners and people we work with; health and wellbeing; and strengthening/broadening partnerships (movements & coalitions). (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic.

RNW Media and SMEX will further develop a set of activities and as a result of mutually sharing experiences, knowledge and skills on digital safety and security will be mutually enhanced. RNW Media will also explore opportunities to collaborate with FEMALE and the strategic partner. Also, as a result of RNW Media's support the consortium partners will further develop protecting and safeguarding approaches. The Oxfam Novib Civic Space team will work with the consortium partners - in particular the stratgic partner and FEMALE - on civic space issues such as collective and individual wellbeing as well as alliance building. The well-being trajectory aims to integrate well-being practices into Masarouna's work and take into account personal lives to increase safety of activists and their movements worked with in Masarouna. The objective for 2024 is that the strategic partner, SMEX and FEMALE have a better understanding of how to foster wellbeing and to prevent/counter factors attacking wellbeing at individual and collective levels, and are able to develop strategies for integrating collective and individual wellbeing in its activities. We are planning a specific learning event, which shall enable cross-country learning on topics related to SRHR and Civic Space. Within the frame of the religious leaders trajectory, lessons on good practices in engaging religious leaders will be drawn and shared with all Masarouna partners. (No quantitative targets added to avoid double counting for same organisations in previous years.)

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, FEMALE reported increased capacity on Civic space risk mitigation and protection of staff, and SMEX reported increased capacity on Strengthen/broaden partnerships while the Strategic Partner maintained its capacity in 2024 (they all realized an actual for KI-13 in 2023).

RNW Media in collaboration with SMEX, FEMALE and the Strategic Partner will develop a set of activities aimed at mutually sharing experiences, as a result of which their knowledge and skills on digital safety and security will be mutually enhanced. The Oxfam Novib Civic Space Team, in collaboration with country team Masarouna leads, partners and consortium partners will bring the Wellbeing Learning Trajectory to a close. As part of that we will draw out and share lessons on good practice and approaches used to integrate awareness of, and steps towards, organisational & individual wellbeing in a programme, illustrating this with practical examples of strategies and actions taken.The team will also bring together lessons and reflections from different trajectories in collaboration with the teams involved and will explore how to best draw out lessons on navigating civic space and backlash, building on learning shared during the Global Learning Event.

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, one both women- and youth-led organisation realised an actual against KI-13 in 2025. FEMALE reported increased capacity on Civic space risk mitigation and protection of staff, partners and people we work with and Perception by and relation with constituency in 2025, resulting in an actual based on the criteria agreed on. The quantitative actual for FEMALE is not reported in the KI-13 quantitative column nor in IATI, as it was already reported in IATI the same year under KI-12. Moreover, one both women and youth led Regional Platform partner increased capacity on Strengthen/broaden partnerships, movements and coalitions in 2025, while SMEX reported increased capacity on Health and Wellbeing. However, these improvements did not result in achieving an actual for KI-13 in 2025 based on the criteria agreed on. The Strategic Partner maintained its capacity in relation to civic space influencing in 2025.

RNW Media, Oxfam Novib and SMEX will further develop a set of activities and as a result of mutually sharing experiences, knowledge and skills on digital safety and security will be enhanced. Also, as a result of RNW Media's support the consortium partners will further develop protecting and safeguarding approaches.
The Oxfam Novib Civic Space team will work with consortium partners and country teams on civic space issues and well being. The well-being trajectory aims to integrate well-being practices into our work and personal lives to increase safety of activists as this is a topic that emerged as a priority for partners.
The regional strategic partner aims to increase their own civic space influencing in 2023, in particular on digital safety and security (delivered by SMEX).
By participation in RNW Media's training, Fe-Male will enhance their capacity on civic space influencing.

In relation to civic space influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, three both women and youth-led organizations (FEMALE, SMEX and the strategic partner) realized an actual for KI-13 in 2023. FEMALE reported increased capacity in Understanding and navigating civic space; Protection in digital space, Health and well-being, Strengthen/broadening partnerships, and Perception by and relation with constituency in 2023, resulting in an actual in 2023 against a target in 2022. The strategic partner reported increased capacity for health and wellbeing in 2022 and protection in digital space in 2023, resulting in an actual increase in 2023 against the target in 2023. SMEX reported increased capacity for understanding and navigating civic space in 2022 and health and well-being in 2023, resulting in an actual increase in 2023 against the target in 2023. The actual for the strategic partner is reported in IATI for KI-13 in 2023, as this is the first time the strategic partner achieves an actual for 1 of the 3 capacity strengthening KIs, While the actual for FEMALE and SMEX is not reported in IATI as they are already included under KI-12 and KI-6 respectively in 2023.

Based on the baseline survey results and initial consultations, Oxfam Novib global team plans to provide capacity strengthening on civic space influencing for organizations engaged at global/regional level.

Regional consortium partner Fe-Male, and the regional strategic partner joined the programme in 2022, and hence were not yet involved in the analysis of the "before/now" assessment of their capacities with the CATool (Fe-Male had a target for 2022; the regional strategic partner not yet). However, the organisations expressed interest in (further) improving the following capacity topics: Understanding and navigating civic space, Civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, Protection in digital space, and other capacities. And indicated currently offer support to others on Civic space risk mitigation & protection of staff, Strengthen/broaden partnerships, and health and wellbeing. (Source: CATool 2022) Regional consortium partner SMEX did not have a target for 2022 yet for this KI. Among activities related to capacity strengthening on civic space influencing reported on for 2022 are the following . SMEX provided Female, the regional strategic partner and partner of Oxfam in country with a Digital Security Audit. The process started an interview to collect basic information about the 3 organisations, then was followed by an assesment to evaluate the digital security level of each organization. These Audits were completed with a full report done based on an digital assessment. Capacity building plans targeting safe online communication are envisioned for 2023.

description.narrative: LTO 1: Decision-makers have formulated (and implemented where possible) policies, and/or removed/amended harmful policies, to enable young people to enjoy their SRHR.
KI-1a # Private sector company policies blocked, adopted and/or improved to enable diverse young people to enjoy their SRHR

comment.narrative: SMEX will undertake research in 2023 to determine the level of restrictions and which private sector companies to target first.
SMEX will undertake research in 2023 to determine the level of restrictions and which private sector companies to target first.
Qualitative information on the private sector company policy concerned is included in the final report.

SMEX has completed a preliminary research draft titled "From Sharing to Silence: Assessing Social Media Suppression of SRHR Content in MENA." This research focuses on five social media platforms. It aims to examine the community guidelines and content moderation practices of platforms concerning SRHR-related content in the MENA region. The study seeks to understand how these platforms handle such content in theory and practice and the impact of their policies. SMEX also intends to have private meetings with the companies to discuss relevant findings on their internal policies affecting SRHR. Unfortunately, a session titled "SRHR Policies on Social Media in the MENA Region" at RightsCon 2023 was delayed due to visa issues. Nonetheless, SMEX participated in RightsCon and voiced concerns about policy deployment in the MENA region, particularly focusing on Instagram's SRHR policies in advertisements. Through its helpdesk, SMEX provided support for 14 cases from various MENA region countries until June 2023, with cases involving online harassment, compromised accounts, and security tips. These cases contributed valuable insights for the research.
Update Oct. 2023: In collaboration with research institutes and potentially consortium and implementing partners, RNW Media produces studies that research on data-backed disconnect between platforms' policy and enforcement, as well as influence other studies in the field. Involve consortium members and implementing partners in existing study on Facebook censorship related to SRHR ads in order to contribute to the necessary policy changes on the relevant platforms

RNW Media reported that Meta has rewritten its global ads policy for Facebook, allowing sexual health, wellness and reproductive ads. Meta states that “ads that promote sexual health, wellness and reproductive products and services” are allowed, and cites several new examples e.g. menopause, pain relief during sex, sex education.
